clues: Constantine was proclaimed Roman emperor here in 306 AD.
Its medieval walls are the longest surviving town walls in England.
The Jorvik Viking Centre here recreates the 10th-century Norse town.
The Shambles, a crooked medieval street, is its best-known lane.
Its Minster is one of northern Europe's largest Gothic cathedrals; the city stands where the Ouse and Foss meet.
